title: Cross-functional roadmap alignment sync - prep notes (Mar 2025)
content:
Meeting: Cross-functional roadmap alignment sync (Product + Eng + Applied ML)
Date/time: 2025-03-12 10:00am PT (30-45m)
Attendees (TBC): Aisha Patel (PM), Michael Chen (Eng - serving runtime), Laura Gomez (Applied ML), Daniel Brooks (SRE/Infra), optionally Priya Rao (product-dedicated)
Purpose: Quick alignment before end-of-quarter sprint planning. Surface dependencies between product priorities and ML model work, clarify rollout gating criteria, and capture action items.

Agenda (rough)
- 0-5m: quick context and goals for the meeting (why we need alignment now)
- 5-15m: product priorities that are time-sensitive (hosted API SLA improvements, dedicated throughput guarantees, model catalog expansion)
- 15-30m: engineering and applied-ML constraints/risks (KV cache changes, quantized model rollout, evaluation metrics)
- 30-40m: decisions needed and next steps / action items

Background/context notes (to bring into the convo)
- Product goal for Q2: reduce 95p latency for generation requests >1k tokens by 30% for hosted API customers on standard tier. Also launch 2 additional verified open-model variants optimized for low-cost inference.
- Applied ML work: Laura's team has ML-108 tracking quantized-compatibility tests; initial results show ~5-7% quality regression for some instruction-following prompts on 4-bit quant. Need more evals.
- Eng/serving runtime: Michael reports that kernel selection improvements and a new batching heuristic can reduce tail latency, but require a short maintenance window and a canary rollout plan.
- Infra: Daniel flagged capacity planning for Dedicated customers; autoscaler tweaks may be needed if we increase guaranteed throughput.

Key discussion points I want to raise
1) Priority tradeoffs: do we prioritize latency improvement (platform changes) or model catalog expansion (model onboarding + eval) this sprint? Both are flagged as high ROI but resource-constrained.
2) Rollout gating: what are the minimal evaluation pass criteria for shipping quantized model variants to hosted API? (accuracy thresholds, regression tests, sample prompts).
3) Canary strategy: define canary % traffic, telemetry signals to watch (latency P95/P99, error rate, model quality metrics), and rollback criteria.
4) Dedicated customers: timeline for autoscaler changes and whether that needs a separate sprint or can be part of the same rollout.

Open questions / unknowns (to surface)
- Applied ML: which prompt sets are authoritative for quality checks? (Laura - confirm list of evaluation prompt sets and owner)
- Engineering: rough estimate for maintenance window length and expected user impact for kernel/batching deploys? (Michael)
- SRE/Infra: any quotas or capacity reservations that would block a canary for Dedicated? (Daniel)

Proposed tentative decisions for the meeting (so we can aim to land on them)
- Ship latency-focused runtime improvements this sprint as a platform priority; split team so a small squad focuses on kernel/batching changes and another on model onboarding.
- Define quantized model gating: pass automated regen tests + no more than 3% regression on weighted eval set; require approval from applied-ML lead before rollout.
- Canary plan: 1% traffic for 48 hours with realtime dashboards; rollback if P99 latency increases by >15% or error rate >0.5% or quality regression on live prompts detected.

Risks / mitigations
- Risk: quantization causes user-visible regressions on edge prompts. Mitigation: keep model-variant behind flag for early customers, require manual signoff and expanded eval set.
- Risk: runtime changes introduce a transient spike in latency during deployment. Mitigation: blue/green with traffic shifting, small-batch canary, and staged kernel enablement.
- Risk: Dedicated autoscaler changes cause capacity overcommit. Mitigation: run stress tests in staging and notify top 5 Dedicated customers ahead of time.

Action items (capture with owner + due date)
1) Laura to share canonical eval prompt sets and a recommended pass/fail rubric by 2025-03-14. (Laura Gomez)
2) Michael to produce a short ops plan for the kernel/batching deploy, including estimated maintenance window and rollback steps, by 2025-03-13. Also include a telemetry dashboard stub. (Michael Chen)
3) Daniel to validate Dedicated autoscaler constraints and give a go/no-go for including autoscaler tweaks in the same sprint by 2025-03-14. (Daniel Brooks)
4) Aisha to align priority sequencing with product leadership and update roadmap doc + confluence page by 2025-03-16. (Aisha Patel)
5) Create a small canary monitoring runbook with explicit metrics and alert thresholds; draft by 2025-03-13 and iterate after sync. (Michael + Laura)
6) Tag the relevant Jira tickets (PROD-342, ML-108) with 'roadmap-q2' and link to this doc. (Aisha)

Notes to self / meeting facilitation tips
- Keep the meeting strict to 30m if possible; follow-up deep dives can be scheduled with sub-teams.
- Use the agenda to force a decision: insist we leave with owners and due dates for the 3 top items.
- Bring up potential customer communications if we expect any Dedicated customer impact.
- Remind applied-ML team that human-in-the-loop checks may be needed for the initial quantized release.

Post-meeting follow-up (what I'll send after the sync)
- 1) Brief meeting summary + decisions + action items to this doc and to the product slack channel.
- 2) Update Jira tickets with owners/due dates.
- 3) Schedule separate deep-dive with SRE + infra if Daniel flags blocking items.

Appendix: quick links / references
- Confluence roadmap page: https://confluence.redwood.ai/pages/ROADMAP-2025
- Jira: PROD-342 (latency initiative), ML-108 (quantization evaluation)
